text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Child support bill may be killed: Renegade Liberal senator Cools joins with Conservatives to fight changes in payments.
- Young Canadians lack elite skills, science test finds: Alberta only jurisdiction to exceed expectations set by composite panel.
- Privatize Ontario Place, MPPs say: Convention centre also on Tories' list.
- Toronto to be host of hostage summit: Japan, Peru seek common strategy.
- Bhutto says vote has been rigged: Trailing in polls, former Pakistani PM not prepared to accept results if beaten.
- Provinces go soft on health-care goals: National debate on medicare urged.
- Blackburn selling media assets: London, Ont., family seeking offers for newspaper, radio station, community publications.
- Tiny Craig Broadcast thinks big: Manitoba media firm scored a huge victory over rival CanWest, winning two Alberta TV licences. And the family venture says it's not through yet.
- Talisman looks around for bargains: Acquisitions could top $1-billion.
- Bombardier seeks buyer for Nova Bus: Won't raise stake in transit bus maker.
- Barshefsky rattles sabre at Canada: U.S. trade czar takes aim at culture, wheat and a host of other irritants.
- Teck and Newmount eye joint bid for Busang.
